title: Ecommerce docs
intro: Ecommerce is the whole shop of your own website: catalog, variants and stock, cart and checkout, orders with your own statuses, delivery, couriers, taxes, promotions, loyalty, returns, reviews, wishlist, alerts, reports, catalog SEO and feeds. Every product, order and customer record is kept in your own database, and media in your own storage (Connections). Shoppers order as guests or signed in with Accounts, payments go through Payments and messages through Notifications, each with its server token pasted into Connections. Your website's tokens are in the Portal: open the website, then Install and tokens. The browser token is public and goes into your pages; the server token is secret and stays on your server.
localhost: Testing on your own computer: the browser token also works on pages served from localhost, *.localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1], on any port, over http or https. These pages use your website's real database, storage, Payments, Notifications and courier keys, so orders placed there are real orders, payments are real payments and messages reach real people. There is no test mode: use your payment gateway's own test keys in Payments if it has them, and delete test orders afterwards.
install: Add the script to every page of your shop, then place each widget where it belongs. A widget renders nothing while its feature is off, the product is stopped or your database is not connected. Every word the widgets show can be changed in Settings → Texts, and their look in Settings → Theme.
attributes: Data attributes of the visitor widgets:

widgets.product_grid: Product listing with filters, sorting, search, page numbers and result totals.
widgets.product_page: The product page blocks: gallery with variant photos, video, variant picker, price and stock, buy box, size guide, FAQs and reviews.
widgets.cart: The cart, checkout and the success page after payment.
widgets.my_orders: The shopper's orders with tracking, invoices and returns.
widgets.alerts_stop: The page an alert message's stop link opens ({stopUrl}): the shopper stops their back-in-stock and price-drop alerts. Make the page at /alerts/unsubscribe/<token> (or the alerts setting stopUrl) and place this widget on it.
widgets.catalog_admin: Products, categories, brands, attributes, stock and media.
widgets.orders_admin: Orders, status moves, shipments, refunds and returns.
widgets.promotions_admin: Coupons, deals, bundles and loyalty points.
widgets.customers_admin: Customers and the blocklist, review moderation, reports and CSV.

jsApi: window.SSEcommerce is ready once the script has loaded. identify(signIn) passes the shopper's Accounts sign-in to the widgets (identify(null) on sign-out). addToCart({ productId, variantId?, quantity? }) adds to the cart; cart.count() and cart.onChange(listener) feed your own header's cart badge. The cart lives in the shopper's browser and is priced by the server on every quote and again when the order is placed.
addToCart: Other scripts on the page add to the cart with a cancelable window event. Chat's product cards use it: when an Ecommerce widget handled the event it calls preventDefault() and opens the cart; otherwise the product's page opens instead.
growthEvents: For Growth (analytics and pixels), the shopper widgets dispatch window events, not cancelable, that Growth's page script listens for; no Growth token is needed. ss:view_item when the product page shows a product, ss:add_to_cart whenever a line is added to the cart (product page, wishlist, addToCart() and the add-to-cart event), ss:begin_checkout the first time the shopper presses Place order, and ss:purchase once the order is placed. The detail is { currency, value, items } (ss:purchase adds orderId and orderNumber, and its value is the order total); each item is { id, variantId, name, price, quantity }, with money in minor units.
signIn: Shoppers browse, fill their cart and see prices without signing in. Placing an order follows the checkout setting guests: off (the default) needs an Accounts sign-in; on lets anyone order with a name and phone; unless_password asks a phone that belongs to an Accounts user with a password to sign in (403 sign_in_required with signIn: member_phone, checked with your Accounts token). A guest sends customer { name, phone, email? } with the order: the phone with its country code (the checkout settings defaultCallingCode and trunkPrefix complete local numbers) and, with the setting countries, of one of those countries (422 country_not_allowed). A guest order's answer carries orderKey once: 32 characters that Ecommerce keeps only as a hash. Keep it in the shopper's browser and send it in the SS-Order-Key header to read the order (GET /v1/shop/orders/<id> or /by-number/<number>), pay, cancel, send a transfer proof, open its invoice, download its files and, with reviews per order_line, review its items; a wrong key reads like a missing order (404). A guest who orders with a phone that a member's record has orders as that member (their blocklist, open-order cap and orders list). The orders list, invoices, return claims, the wishlist, loyalty and reviews per product need a sign-in, and alerts too unless the alerts setting guests is on. To sign shoppers in, paste your website's Accounts server token into Connections, put the Accounts widgets on your site and pass the sign-in to SSEcommerce.identify(signIn). Ecommerce verifies each sign-in with your Accounts keys and keeps only shop records (orders, loyalty, blocklist) linked to the Accounts user id. When a signed-in shopper whose phone Accounts verified orders or opens their orders, the guest orders, loyalty points and alerts of that phone move to them.
payments: Payment methods are set in Settings → Checkout and payment (online, bank transfer and pay at pickup) and with Cash on delivery, its own feature; the cart lists them in the order of the checkout setting paymentOrder (by default online, bank transfer, cash on delivery, then pay at pickup), preselects the first available and shows your note for each (noteCod, noteOnline, noteBankTransfer, notePickup). Cash on delivery and pay at pickup orders start where your order flow's starts say (awaiting confirmation by default; a start in an open status confirms them at once). Online payments go through Payments: paste your website's Payments server token into Connections. The order starts awaiting payment, the shopper pays on Payments' page, and Ecommerce marks the order paid only after Payments says it was paid for the order's exact amount and currency. Bank transfers go through Payments' bank page too; with the checkout setting bankTransferVia manual the order waits with no Payments payment, shows your bank details, takes the shopper's proof and your staff record the payment (see Bank transfers and transfer proofs). While Payments is connected, bank transfer is offered only once its bank details are saved there (or its Require bank details is off). A cash on delivery advance is a Payments payment for the advance, or with the cod setting advanceVia manual a transfer your staff record. An order waiting for its payment is canceled when the checkout setting paymentWindowMinutes ends, and one waiting for confirmation when confirmationHours ends (0 = never for either); this is checked when your shop is used, never in the background. Once the shopper sends a transfer proof the order no longer ends with its payment window: it waits for your staff to record the payment and confirm it, or cancel it. A waiting payment is checked again when the order is read (at most every 30 seconds) and before a waiting order is canceled at the end of its window. When an order is canceled (by you, the shopper or the end of its window), edited, deleted (one or all) or paid by hand (a payment your staff record) before it is paid, its Payments payment is canceled too, so it can no longer be paid; if the shopper paid just before, the order stays and is marked paid. A delete or a payment by hand waits while Payments cannot be reached, so try again. Money that still reaches Payments after a cancel is recorded on the canceled order, which shows a refund due; refund it from the order. Refunds of orders paid online are made through Payments; when Payments can only record a refund (bank transfers, some gateways), the order says so and you return the money yourself. Send the total the shopper saw as expectedTotal with the order: a different total answers 409 price_changed with the new quote.
success: After paying, Payments sends the shopper back to the address your page sent with the order as returnUrl (on your site), with ss_order=<order id> added; the cart widget sends its own page and then shows the order's result (paid, waiting or failed). Without returnUrl the checkout settings successUrl and cancelUrl are used (with {number} and {id}), else your home page with ss_order. Never treat the return itself as a payment: only the order's status counts.
orderFlow: Orders move through your own statuses (Settings → Orders and messages, or PUT /v1/lists/order_flow). You name the statuses (keys of 2–40 lower-case letters, digits, _ or -), add your own (up to 30) and choose the allowed moves; each status has a role (its kind of step), and the rules of the roles hold whatever the flow, so stock, offer uses, loyalty points and money stay right. A flow has exactly one awaiting_payment status, at most one awaiting_confirmation status (without one, cash on delivery, pickup and free orders start in an open status) and at least one open, delivered and canceled status. Each status also has the name shoppers read (shopperLabel, else its name), a line per payment method shoppers read under it (shopperText: cod, online, bank_transfer, pickup) and whether entering it sends the shopper a message (notify). Each move says who may make it (who: staff; staff and shopper, a cancel before dispatch; or system, only the shop itself), the permission a ticket needs (orders.manage, into a refunded status always orders.refund), what staff give with it (needs: note, reason — a note for the shopper —, units — every serial number) and its options (see Order flow options). triggers name the statuses the shop moves orders to by itself and starts where orders that need no payment first start. A flow saved without these reads with today's behavior. The default flow, with the moves out of each status:

roles.awaiting_payment: Paid online, by bank transfer or with a cash on delivery advance: waits for the payment (confirmed by Payments, or recorded by your staff); moved to the flow's paid status once Payments confirms it (its paid trigger), canceled when the time to pay ends (its windowEnd).
roles.awaiting_confirmation: Cash on delivery and pay at pickup, and free online or bank-transfer orders, by default (the flow's starts may start them in an open status, a free one also in awaiting payment, already paid, with no time to pay): waits for your staff to confirm; canceled when the time to confirm ends (to the flow's windowEnd status).
roles.open: Confirmed and being prepared. A move out of waiting into an open, packed or shipped status whose option paidOnConfirm lists the order's payment method records its balance as paid when staff make it.
roles.packed: Packed: serial numbers are captured here with Grades and serials, and the dispatch video as the move's video option says (off, optional or required); staff may replace the video while the order is packed or shipped (PATCH /v1/orders/<id> { video }).
roles.shipped: Handed to the courier: the move takes the courier and the tracking number (required unless the move's tracking option is optional), or books the shipment with Courier APIs; with typed serial numbers, every unit's number first when the move needs units (the default).
roles.delivered: Delivered: loyalty points are credited, reviews open, return windows start, and cash on delivery and pay at pickup orders are marked paid (unless the cod setting paidOnDelivery is off).
roles.cancelled: Stock, booked slots, offer uses and redeemed points go back exactly once; money paid through Payments is refunded when staff cancel and the move's refund option is auto (the default; staff: it shows as a refund due), and money your staff recorded shows as a refund due. A shopper's cancel follows its move's shopperPaid option. A cancel after delivery or of a closed order (an extra move you list) puts the items back in stock only as the move's restock says (default no) and takes earned points back unless its points option is keep.
roles.returned_to_origin: The package came back. The move takes reason rto (the default; it counts towards the customer's returned-package flag, the cod setting rtoThreshold) or customer_return (not counted). Stock goes back as the move's restock option says (yes, the default; no keeps it out; ask: staff send restock with each move); offer uses and points stay spent.
roles.returned: A customer's return after delivery: stock goes back as the move's restock says, earned points are taken back unless its points option is keep, and redeemed points are given back.
roles.refunded: The money was returned (the share paid through Payments through Payments, the rest recorded). Moving here needs orders.refund on a ticket. Before delivery it acts as a cancel and needs something paid (else 409 nothing_paid, unless the move's unpaid option is cancel: then it cancels with no money). After delivery the items go back in stock only as the move's restock says (default no) and earned points are taken back unless its points option is keep. With the flow's refundsCover trigger, an order whose refunds reach what was paid moves here by itself when the flow lists the move.

messages: Messages to shoppers go through Notifications: paste your website's Notifications server token into Connections. Every message below goes out with Ecommerce's default words (US English) by email and SMS until you write your own template in Notifications (Settings → Templates, where you can also switch a message off on a channel); WhatsApp has no default words, so it needs your WhatsApp template approved at Meta. Order messages are optional: choose the channels (messageChannels) in Settings → Orders and messages, and which statuses send a message in your order flow (each status's notify). A failed or unconnected send never stops an order. Order and claim messages and staff alerts are sent as required (a shopper's opt-out does not stop them) and saved in your database first: when Notifications does not take one, it is tried again on your shop's next uses (1, 5, 15 and 60 minutes later, then every 3 hours) for up to a day, and a message that got through is never sent twice. The order templates:
couriers: Couriers are a list in Settings → Couriers: a name and a tracking link template in which {tracking} is replaced by the tracking number (for example https://track.courier.example/?id={tracking}). Staff pick the courier and enter the tracking number when an order ships, and the shopper gets the link.
courierApi: With Courier APIs on, Ecommerce books the shipment with your courier's own API and reads its latest status, using your keys (Connections → Courier API keys). The connection is one generic adapter for any courier: the booking address (Ecommerce posts the JSON body built from your template), the tracking address with {tracking}, your API key, optional extra headers as a JSON object of text values (they may hold {apiKey}; without them the key goes as Authorization: Bearer <key>), the booking body template, and where the tracking number (default trackingNumber) and the status (default status) are in the courier's JSON answers, as dotted paths. In the body template, {number}, {name}, {phone}, {email}, {line1}, {line2}, {city}, {area}, {postalCode}, {country}, {items}, {amount} (decimal), {total} (minor units), {cod} (the decimal to collect, 0 when prepaid), {currency} and {note} are filled in, JSON-escaped. There is nothing to register at the courier: Ecommerce calls the courier, never the other way round.
storage: Product images, downloads and return photos are kept in your own S3-compatible bucket (Connections → Storage). Uploads go from the browser straight to the bucket with a short presigned PUT, so the bucket's CORS must allow PUT (and GET) from your website's origin and from your admin page's origin. Then set the public address of your images (catalog setting mediaBaseUrl: a public bucket or a CDN in front of it) so images have lasting addresses and pages load faster; until then the media route under Your site serves gives search engines lasting addresses. Product photos should be at least 500 × 500 pixels (shopping catalogs refuse smaller ones from Jan 31, 2027; about 1500 × 1500 is best): the catalog admin widget warns when one is smaller. The CORS rule:
site: Some things must be served from your own domain: the sitemap, product meta tags and structured data, your images' lasting addresses (until your bucket has a public address), product feeds, llms.txt and your policy pages. Your site fetches them from the API with the server token (never from the browser) and serves them; the snippets below are Next.js route handlers and pages, and any server can do the same with a plain HTTPS request.

siteRoutes.media: Your images at addresses that never change, for search engines, sitemaps and shopping catalogs (a signed link lasts an hour, so it is never in them). With the catalog setting mediaBaseUrl (the public address of your bucket or CDN; best, set it right after connecting storage) every image uses it and you need no route. Without it, SEO answers, sitemaps and feeds name https://<your domain><mediaPath>/<signature>/<key> (mediaPath /media by default): serve that path with this route, which asks GET /v1/media for a 5-minute link to the file (only for keys Ecommerce named) and serves it with a one-year cache. Name the folder after your mediaPath. The shop's widgets keep showing images through signed links until the public address is set; Shop health says so (images_short_lived).
siteRoutes.sitemap: The sitemap of your categories, indexable landing and glossary pages and products, with their images (SEO); pages marked noindex and pages whose canonical address is another page are left out. Above the seo setting sitemapSize addresses (10,000 by default) the answer is a sitemap index whose files are your sitemap address with ?file=categories, ?file=landings, ?file=products-1 and so on; the route below fetches each file from GET /v1/seo/sitemaps/<file>. The index uses the seo setting sitemapUrl (/sitemap.xml by default) as your sitemap address. Add Sitemap: https://<your domain>/sitemap.xml to your robots.txt.
siteRoutes.feedXml: The product feed for shopping and social catalogs (Feeds), as XML.
siteRoutes.llms: llms.txt of your catalog for AI assistants (llms.txt).
siteRoutes.llmsFull: llms-full.txt: every product in stock with its price range, by category, with the grades of each category (llms.txt, with the llms_txt setting full on; 404 otherwise).

productMeta: GET /v1/seo/products/<id or slug> answers { title, description, canonical, image, robots, focusKeyword, jsonLd } for your product page: the meta tags, robots (from the product's noindex and nofollow) and the JSON-LD structured data (a ProductGroup with its variants, as a string safe to put in a script tag). An earlier slug, a slug in other letter case or an archived product sent to its category (retiredUrl) answers { moved: { slug, url } } instead: answer it with a 308 to url. GET /v1/seo/categories/<id or slug> answers the same for a category page (with status coming_soon and robots noindex while it is coming soon).
listing: GET /v1/seo/listing?category=<id or slug>&brand=&grade=&page=&… answers what a listing page (a category, a landing page, or any filtered list) puts in its head and above the grid: { h1, title, description, intro, faqs, canonical, robots, landing, jsonLd } (CollectionPage, ItemList of the products the page shows and BreadcrumbList; a FAQPage only with the seo setting faqMarkup on). robots is index only for a category and its pages without other filters and for an indexable landing page; any other filter or a sort is noindex, follow, so filtered lists never compete with your category pages. canonical is the page's own address: pages 2, 3 … add page=<n>, and a filtered list names itself with its filters in one order (by name). Pass your page's query as it is (page, limit and sort as the grid takes them); an earlier category slug answers { moved } like a product.
policies: GET /v1/policies answers { format, shipping, returns, privacy, terms, warranty } from Settings → Policies, for your own policy pages: empty policies are left out, and {returnDays}, {warrantyDays}, {warrantyMonths}, {business}, {email}, {phone}, {address} (from business.json), {deliveryFee} and {freeDeliveryOver} (the delivery fee where no zone matches and the amount delivery is free from, as money) are filled in, also written with double braces ({{business}}). With the checkout setting policyFormat html the texts are HTML cleaned by Ecommerce to p, br, strong, em, u, ul, ol, li, h2, h3, h4, blockquote and links (https, on your site, mailto: or tel:):
chat: Chat's shop tools read your shop through these lookups with your website's Ecommerce server token (paste it into Chat's Connections). They only read. The me/* lookups take the visitor's Accounts sign-in forwarded in the SS-Sign-In header; Ecommerce verifies it with Accounts. Every product answer gives the price shoppers see on the product page (after the best live item deal on one unit, as the cart prices it) with compareAtPrice, the price struck through above it, and the deal in it with its savings; the price filters compare the variants' own prices, as shop listings do. The quote prices the cart: price is the variant's own price, priceAfterDeals what the cart charges a unit, and compareAtPrice the variant's own "was" price when higher.
chatRoutes: GET /v1/chat/products?q=<text>&category=<id or slug>&grade=<keys>&minPrice=&maxPrice=&inStock=1&limit=5: search the catalog by words and filters (up to 12 results; with filters the words may be left out), each at the price on the product page
GET /v1/chat/products/<productId>: one product's details, each variant with its grade, price on the product page, stock left and warranty
GET /v1/chat/products/<productId>/quote?variantId=&quantity=1-5&paymentMethod=&city=: the price as the cart prices it, with deals, fees, delivery and the free-delivery threshold
GET /v1/chat/deals?limit=10: active deals with their badge, discount label, color, banner and hours
GET /v1/chat/products/top?kind=top|new&limit=5: best sellers or new products
GET /v1/chat/me/orders?limit=5 (SS-Sign-In): the visitor's orders with their lines, amount due, tracking note, expected date and dispatch video
GET /v1/chat/me/account (SS-Sign-In): the visitor's first name, loyalty points, city and area
GET /v1/chat/me/shipments (SS-Sign-In): the visitor's shipments with tracking links, notes and expected dates

GET /v1/chat/context?productId= (SS-Sign-In optional): the live store context for AI replies: policies, the 10 newest products with their price per grade as the product page shows it, the deals table, the product named and the visitor's first name, city and points, as data and as one text of at most 6,000 characters
customers: A customer is named by their customer id (cus_…, in every customer answer as id; guests have no Accounts user) or a member's Accounts user id, in GET and PATCH /v1/customers/<id>, POST /v1/customers/<id>/seen and the loyalty routes /v1/loyalty/accounts/<id>; a guest's orders, spend and points are theirs by customer id, and a guest who orders with a phone a member's record has orders as that member. Opening an Accounts user who has not ordered yet makes their record (joined when Accounts says), so staff can note or block them; with the checkout setting customerRecords: sign_in a signed-in shopper's record is made at their first visit. GET /v1/customers?userIds=<up to 100 Accounts user ids, comma-separated> gives what a page of your own member list ordered and spent. Accounts shows a shopper's orders in its Orders tab, and Chat in its context panel, with GET /v1/customers/<Accounts user id or customer id>/orders?limit= (server token):
dataRights: Data rights run through Accounts: when a user asks for their data or to be deleted, Accounts calls each product. Ecommerce finds the person's records by Accounts user id, email or phone; an export lists their orders and customer record as the shopper sees them (never unit costs, staff notes or names, or a block and its reason), returns, reviews, wishlist, alerts and loyalty history, and a deletion erases them (with the order messages and staff alerts about them still waiting to be sent) or, where you must keep an order for your accounts, removes the personal details from it. Staff actions in the admin widgets are copied to the Accounts activity log.
admin: Admin widgets run in your own admin with a ticket. Include the script without data-token, place the widgets and register your ticket function. The widget calls it at start and 1 minute before the ticket expires; your server checks the user's sign-in and role every time and asks only for the permissions that user has.
tickets: Your server asks for a ticket with the server token (never send the server token to a browser). The origin is the address of your admin page: any https origin, or a local one while testing. Tickets last 15 minutes and carry only the permissions of switched-on features. Permissions:
kit: In Ecommerce: the lists are order_flow, couriers, delivery_zones, tax_rules, grades, booking_hours and role_prices (GET and PUT /v1/lists/<list> with { value }, checked like the dashboard's editors). Counts: orders (/v1/orders/count and /counts?by=status|role|paymentMethod|paymentState; role groups the status keys by their role in your order flow), products (by=status|brand|stockState|featured|grade), customers (by=blocked), reviews and returns (by=status), each with the same filters as its list and an /v1/admin/ twin for the admin widgets. An order move or refund and a return claim step made with SS-Actor headers show that staff member's name in the order's or the claim's history, every change shows it in the activity log (with the order number, product name or code as its label), and a refund through Payments names them there too. Every visitor route under /v1/shop/ takes the server token with SS-Sign-In and SS-Visitor-IP. Totals and prices in messages, invoices, packing slips, llms.txt and the Chat lookups (priceText, totalText) follow your Format; order numbers take the year in your business time zone, and report days are days in that time zone.
business: Every product reads your business basics (name, contact, address) from https://<your domain>/.well-known/business.json. Only name is required; without the file the name is your domain. Shop-only details (payment methods, delivery, policies) are Ecommerce settings.
api: Every route answers JSON (feeds, sitemaps, llms.txt, CSV files and the HTML invoices, packing slips and pick lists answer their own formats); errors are RFC 9457 problems with a stable code. Amounts are integer minor units of your shop currency. Times are ISO 8601 in UTC. Lists are paged with cursor and limit. Routes that create things or move money take an Idempotency-Key header (placing an order needs one). Routes of a feature that is off answer 403 feature_off. Each route below links to its full description: its parameters, the fields it takes and the fields it answers.

catalogSeo.intro: What the catalog and its SEO can do beyond the basics, each with the feature it needs. Routes are named with the server token; every staff route also has its /v1/admin/ twin for the admin widgets (ticket with catalog.edit), and the catalog admin widget edits every field below.

sections.title: Category and brand status and content
paragraphs: Categories have a status: active, coming_soon (listed with their content, their products hidden) or hidden. Brands are active or hidden, and list the categories they belong to (categoryIds; none = every category). A hidden category or brand hides its products from every shopper read, feed, sitemap, llms.txt and Chat lookup, judged on every read, so switching it back shows them again at once.

Categories also carry an icon (a name of at most 40 characters your website maps to its own icon), content { summary, bullets: [{ text, icon }] } with at most 12 bullets, at most 20 FAQs, a size chart, requiresSerial (true, false or null) and the SEO fields; brands carry the SEO fields and a size chart. Earlier slugs are kept in previousSlugs (read-only).

sections.title: Featured products and staff filters
paragraphs: Products have a featured flag; shop listings take featured=1. The staff product list filters by q, status, kind, category, brand (several, comma-separated), lowStock, featured (1 or 0), stockState (none, out, partial or full; several), hasMedia (1 or 0) and grade (several), and its rows add featured, stockState, grades and mediaCount. lowStock=1 keeps products that track stock and are not archived with a variant low on stock: still for sale (offered, not marked sold out) with 1 to the catalog setting lowStock units. Counts take the same filters: /v1/products/count, and /v1/products/counts?by=status, brand, stockState, featured or grade; by=variantStock counts the variants instead, as out, low and in (for a dashboard or a bell).

sections.title: Rich descriptions and HTML policies
paragraphs: A product's descriptionHtml is cleaned when saved to p, br, strong, em, u, ul, ol, li, h3, h4, blockquote and links with an https or site-relative href (at most 20,000 characters); the plain description is then made from it for search, feeds and AI copy. The product page widget builds the page from that cleaned copy.

Policies (Settings → Policies: delivery, returns, privacy, terms and warranty) are plain text or, with the checkout setting policyFormat html, the same cleaned HTML. {returnDays}, {warrantyDays}, {warrantyMonths}, {business}, {email}, {phone}, {address}, {deliveryFee} and {freeDeliveryOver} (one or two braces) are filled in when they are read; other text in braces stays as written, and empty policies are left out.

sections.title: Product video
paragraphs: A product's video is { kind: 'file', key } (an MP4 or WebM uploaded to your storage like a photo, up to the catalog setting videoMaxBytes, 64 MB by default), { kind: 'youtube', id } (a YouTube id or address), { kind: 'url', url } (https) or null. The shop's product answer gives the file's address and type, or the YouTube embed address, and the product page widget plays it.

sections.title: Size charts
paragraphs: With Size charts on, a chart has a name, a unit (in or cm), at most 12 columns { key, label }, at most 40 rows { size, label, values }, fit advice, notes and active. Products, brands and categories take a sizeChartId: a product page shows the product's chart, else its brand's, else its category's, else the size_charts setting defaultChartId (empty by default: none; hideSizeGuide on a product shows none), with an in/cm switch. A chart in use or set as the default cannot be deleted (409); its answer says where it is used.

sections.title: Photo sizes and variant galleries
paragraphs: There is no image processing on the server. The catalog admin widget's uploader makes thumb, card and detail WebP copies of each photo in the browser, uploads each one to your storage and makes a blur image (a data URI of at most 2 kB); the photo is attached with { key, alt, sizes: { thumb, card, detail }, width, height, blur }. Your own uploader can do the same: every key comes from POST /v1/catalog/uploads for that product.

Variants have their own photos (media: at most 24 per variant and 200 per product, keys of the product's uploads); removing a photo from the product removes it from its variants too. Shop answers give each photo's sizes and each variant's photos, and product cards carry cardImages: the first photo of up to 4 variants that look different (a 2×2 grid).

sections.title: Attributes per category, on variants
paragraphs: An attribute has a slug (made from its name when empty; shop filters are attr.<slug>), may be the definition for one category (categoryId: the same slug once per category with its own name, choices, unit, glossary and SEO, and once for every category; a product, a listing and a glossary page take the definition of their category or the nearest category above it first, then the one for every category), the categories it belongs to (none = all), whether it is set on the product or on each variant (on: product or variant; variant attributes are text, number or choice), multiple (several values on one variant), choices { value, label }, visibility (always, or only for some brands, some grades, or when another attribute has a value), how cards show it (none, image or chips), active, and glossary SEO { title, description, body, faqs }.

Variants hold attributes { <attributeId>: value or [values] }, and the product's options are made from them (up to 6 axes; two variants may share options when their grades differ). A product's attribute setup (at most 20 { attributeId, values, customValues, defaultValue }) lists the values it is sold in; Generate adds every missing combination as a variant (at most 250) with the price and stock you give, for one product or up to 100 at once (Variants).

sections.title: Listing filters, page numbers and totals
paragraphs: GET /v1/shop/products filters by q, category, brand and grade (several values, comma-separated), attr.<slug>=a,b, minPrice, maxPrice, inStock, featured=1 and deal=<id or slug>; one active variant must match the price, attributes, grade and stock together. Sorts are newest, price_asc, price_desc, top, sold_asc, rating, name and updated (price ties go to the newest). It pages like every list, with cursor and the answer's nextCursor and hasMore; page (1 to 500) works beside the cursor, and count=1 adds total (exact up to 10,000, else capped is true). Facets carry counts and labels, cards carry priceMax for price ranges and their brand { id, name, slug }, and variants=1 adds each card's active variants { id, options, attributes [{ slug, name, label }], price, compareAtPrice, inStock, grade, url } for websites that draw their own cards (never stock counts). The catalog setting pageSize goes up to 60.

sections.title: Stock display and sold out
paragraphs: The catalog setting showStock (none, low or always) and lowStockShown (5) decide what shoppers are told: shop answers and Chat lookups carry stockLeft per variant (a number, or null when it is not shown), so the product page can say Only 3 left or 12 in stock. A variant marked soldOut is shown as sold out without changing its stock; POST /v1/products/:id/stock takes soldOut alone or with a stock change.

sections.title: Grades per category
paragraphs: Condition grades (Settings → Grades and serials, or PUT /v1/lists/grades) have a key (lower-case letters, digits, _ and -), a name, a description of up to 1,200 characters, return and warranty days, the categories they are for (none = all), a color, a condition video (a file key or a YouTube id), content (summary and bullets), whether they are offered, a condition (new, refurbished or used, used for structured data and feeds instead of the seo setting gradedCondition) and a glossary page's SEO; up to 100 grades. A grade may be one category's definition of its key (categoryId): the same key then exists once per category, with its own name, texts, days and glossary, and once without a category for every other one; a product's variants take the entry of their category or the nearest category above it first. Shop answers give each variant's grade with these details.

sections.title: Serial numbers and the IMEI check
paragraphs: The grades_serials setting serialMode is registered (serial numbers are added to stock first and picked when an order is packed) or typed (typed when an order is packed or later with PATCH /v1/orders/<id> { serials: { <lineId>: ['…'] } }, one per unit, and required before the order moves to a shipped status). serialCheck imei requires 15 digits that pass the IMEI (Luhn) check digit. A category's requiresSerial says whether its products need serial numbers; a product with serialized null follows its categories. Order lines, invoices and the shopper's orders show the serial numbers.

sections.title: Warranty per variant
paragraphs: A variant's warrantyDays (null = the product's, then its grade's, then the returns setting) is kept on the order line when the order is placed; warranty claims use it, and shop answers and invoices show it.

sections.title: Page addresses, slug history and moved pages
paragraphs: The catalog setting productUrl takes {slug} (or {id}), {category} (its first category's slug), {categoryPath} (that category's slugs from the top) and {brand}, for example /{category}/{slug}; categoryUrl takes {slug} or {path}. variantQuery is added to a product's address to open one variant, with {grade} and {attributes} (its slug=value pairs; an attribute with several values names the first), for example grade={grade}&{attributes}. Every link Ecommerce makes follows them: sitemaps, feeds, canonical addresses, structured data, llms.txt, Chat cards, messages and cart lines.

When a product's or category's slug changes, the old one is kept (at most 20 in previousSlugs). Lookups by slug ignore letter case and match old slugs, and then answer { moved: { slug, url } }: your site turns it into a 308 to url (see the product page below). With retiredUrl set to category, an archived product answers moved to its category's page instead of not found.

sections.title: Atlas Search
paragraphs: Basic search matches every word anywhere in the name, summary, tags or SKUs; with the catalog setting searchMatch at phrase, the shop's basic search matches the whole phrase, words in order, in the name or a SKU. With the catalog setting search at atlas, shop and Chat searches use Atlas Search on your own database (chatSearch gives Chat its own mode: same as the shop by default, basic or atlas): fuzzy autocomplete on the product name (one typo allowed), text on the tags and summary, and the brands and categories whose names match, filtered on your website and active products and ranked by score (unless the shopper picks a sort); the listing's other filters follow.

Your database must be on MongoDB Atlas. In Atlas, open your cluster → Atlas Search → Create Search Index → JSON Editor, pick your shop's database and the ss_ecommerce_products collection, name the index as the catalog setting searchIndex (ss_ecommerce_products_search by default) and paste this definition:

A new index is built first: wait until Atlas shows it ready (Status: Active / Queryable) before you switch search to atlas, for example when you move a shop's catalog. If the search fails, or finds nothing while the index finds none of your active products (Atlas answers nothing, without an error, for an index that is missing, named differently or still building), basic search answers instead, and the dashboard's Overview shows Search index missing until a search works again.

sections.title: Landing pages, listing heads and glossary pages
paragraphs: With Landing pages on (it needs SEO), a landing page is a category, brand and grade combination with its own h1, title, description, introduction and FAQs, one per combination (409 for a second). indexable is auto, yes or no; auto is indexed while at least landingMinProducts (3) of its products are in stock (and, while automatic landing pages are on, autoMinInStockVariants (3) of their variants), judged on every read, and answers add url, inStock, inStockVariants and indexed. Its address comes from the setting landingUrl ({categoryUrl}?brand={brand}&grade={grade} by default). With AI copy on, POST /v1/landings/<id>/ai-copy suggests its texts.

Automatic landing pages: with the setting auto at category_brand, every category and brand whose products shoppers may see have at least autoMinProducts (2) products and autoMinInStockVariants (3) variants in stock is a landing page without a record (category_brand_grade adds every category, brand and grade); GET /v1/seo/listing indexes it (landing.automatic true, id null) with the heading and title of the pattern autoTitle ({category} {brand} {grade} by default; also {products}, {variants}, {price} and {storeName}) and the description of autoDescription (empty: the category's or brand's), and the sitemaps list it. A landing page you create for the combination wins. With autoCopy ai (and AI copy on with its key), saving a product writes one of its automatic pages with AI copy as a landing page you can edit; formula (the default) uses the patterns only. Nothing is stored or scheduled: the stock is read with each listing or sitemap read.

GET /v1/seo/listing gives the head of any listing your site shows (see Your site serves): robots is index only for a category (and its pages) and an indexable landing page, noindex for any other filter. Every page keeps its own canonical address; with the seo setting pagedListings noindex, pages 2, 3 … are noindex, follow (index by default).

Glossary pages explain an attribute or a grade from its glossary SEO, at the addresses of the settings attributeUrl ({slug}) and gradeUrl ({key}), both also taking {category} (a category's slug, for example /attributes/{category}/{slug}). Per category, GET /v1/seo/attributes/<category>/<slug> and /v1/seo/grades/<category>/<key> answer the definition of that category or the nearest category above it first, then the one for every category; a grade entry may also be one category's definition (categoryId in the grades list, the same key once per category). Once attributeUrl is set every active attribute's page is listed in the sitemaps (with {category}: a category's definition at its category, one for every category at each category it names), and grades with their own text once gradeUrl is set, as are indexable landing pages. An attribute without its own SEO title or text takes the patterns attributeTitle ({name} by default, for example What is {name}?) and attributeDescription (empty by default) with {name}, {unit}, {values} (its first five choices), {category} (the page's category) and {storeName}.

sections.title: SEO fields, structured data, sitemaps, llms-full.txt and IndexNow
paragraphs: Products, categories and brands have seo { title, description, canonicalUrl, ogImage, noindex, nofollow, focusKeyword, titleMode, source }, and products at most 20 FAQs (AI copy can suggest them). Your own titles and descriptions are used as written: a description is never cut, and with titleMode as_written the title is the whole page title (template: the title pattern goes around it). source says who wrote the copy: merchant (your team), import (your earlier shop's, moved in) or ai (an AI suggestion applied, or written on save); a change of the title or description records merchant unless you send source ai. The seo settings defaultDescription and defaultImage fill pages that have none.

Page titles follow the seo setting titleTemplate ({name} | {business}). Its {name} is a page's own SEO title, else the pattern productTitle or categoryTitle ({name} by default; products take {name}, {brand}, {category}, {storeName} and the facts below, categories {name}, {category} for the category above and {storeName}, for example {brand} {name} or Shop {name}). The name in titles is never added twice: when the page's part already holds it, nothing is added. A product without an SEO description of its own takes its summary when it has 50 characters or more, else the pattern productDescription ({name}[ by {brand}][ — {category}][. {price}][. In stock: {inStockOptions}]. by default), then its description; a category takes categoryDescription (empty by default), then its summary and description. Product patterns take the facts {price} (the price, or the range lowest – highest), {minPrice}, {maxPrice}, {options} and {inStockOptions} (the option values offered, and those in stock), {conditions} (the grades offered) and {topSpecs} (the first 3 specs), filled on every read so they never go stale; variantTitle ({name} - {options}) names each variant in structured data ({name}, {brand}, {options}, {grade}). A part in square brackets is left out when one of its placeholders is empty, for example [ by {brand}]. brandName is the name {business} and {storeName} stand for (empty: your business name). Empty brackets and separators left over are dropped. Pattern copy is never stored.

A product's JSON-LD is a ProductGroup with its variants offered (active and priced above 0; a product with none has no Product node), each with its own photo (else the product's), its SKU (else its feed item id), the condition of its grade and its return policy: the product's return days, else its grade's, else the returns setting (0 = not returnable), given only with the country of your business.json; digital goods and bookings only when the product names its own days. Each offer's price is the price shown (after the best item deal on one unit, as cards and the product page show it), with the higher price as a StrikethroughPrice and, for a deal that holds all day and has an end, validFrom and priceValidUntil (its last day). Shipping details (your default delivery fee, free from the free-delivery amount, to your country) are given only for physical goods and only with delivery days, which Google requires. Up to 5 reviews follow, and a FAQPage only with the seo setting faqMarkup on (Google stopped showing FAQ results on May 7, 2026; the questions are still answered for your page). A category's adds an ItemList of the products on its first page.

Above sitemapSize addresses the sitemap is an index of files (categories, landings, products-1, products-2 …) with image entries, served from GET /v1/seo/sitemaps/<file>. With the llms_txt setting full on, GET /v1/llms-full.txt lists every product in stock with its price range and the grades of each category.

With the seo setting indexNowOnSave on and the Growth token pasted in Connections, the address of a product or category is sent to search engines through Growth's IndexNow right after it is saved. With the seo setting autoSeo at on_save, saving a product (or, with Landing pages on, an attribute) has your AI provider write its empty SEO title, description and FAQs once, when AI copy is on and its key is in Connections; the copy is kept with source ai. Without AI, or when the provider does not answer, nothing is written: the patterns fill the pages on every read.

sections.title: Feed options
paragraphs: Item ids: each variant's own id, or the feedId an import kept from the earlier shop's feed (and the product's imported feedGroupId as item_group_id on every item), so Merchant Center keeps the items it already lists. The feeds settings: googleCategory (sent with every item), gradeLabel (each item's grade name as custom_label_0), itemTitle ({name} - {variant} by default, with {name}, {brand}, {variant} for the options on products with several variants and {options} for the options always), itemDescription (body: the description, else the summary; seo: the SEO description first) and identifierExists (auto: nothing sent; no: identifier_exists no on items without GTIN and MPN). Each item's condition follows its grade, shipping comes from the default delivery fee (0 at or above the free-delivery amount), prices follow your Format with whole units, and variants priced 0 are left out (the catalogs refuse free items). On sale, price is the regular price and sale_price the price shown (after a deal that holds all day, or below a "was" price), with sale_price_effective_date (start/end, ISO 8601) while the deal has an end; the Meta CSV has the same sale_price and sale_price_effective_date columns. A deal limited to weekdays or hours is left out of the feeds (they are read at the catalogs' own pace).

catalog: Set the shop currency, your product, category and variant page addresses and, if your bucket has a public address or CDN, the media address in Settings → Catalog. Connect your database and storage. Manage products with the catalog admin widget and show them with the product grid and product page widgets.

Categories and brands have a status and content, products a featured flag, rich descriptions, a video, SEO fields and FAQs, and earlier slugs keep working; shop listings filter, count and page, show stock as you choose and can search with Atlas Search (see Catalog and SEO).
variants: Give a product options (for example size and color), up to 6; each variant has its own price, stock, SKU, photos, warranty and attributes (several values allowed), and the product page shows a variant picker. Generate adds every missing combination of a product's attribute setup (see Catalog and SEO).
multi_location: Keep stock per location (warehouses, shops). Orders take stock from the first location that has it, in the order you set.
grades_serials: Define condition grades in Settings → Grades and serials: per grade its categories, return and warranty days, color, condition video, content, condition and glossary page. Serial numbers (such as IMEI) are registered in stock and picked when an order is packed, or typed at packing or later and checked as IMEI if you choose; they appear on invoices, packing slips and the shopper's orders (see Catalog and SEO).
digital_goods: Attach files or license keys to a product. The shopper gets the download link or key once the order is paid. Files are kept in your storage.
bookings: Sell services in simple slots: each product has a duration, your weekly booking hours are set in Settings → Catalog, and a slot is never booked twice.
checkout: The cart, checkout and success page (cart widget), My orders (my_orders widget) and the orders admin widget. Shoppers order signed in with Accounts (paste the Accounts token) or, with the checkout setting guests, as guests with an order key. Order statuses and moves, the order number prefix and order messages are in Settings → Orders and messages; couriers and their tracking links in Settings → Couriers; your delivery, returns, privacy, terms and warranty policies, as text or HTML, in Settings → Policies. See Checkout, orders and promotions for payments recorded by hand, more moves, packing, edits, numbers and deletes.
cod: Cash on delivery orders start where your order flow's starts say: awaiting confirmation, or an open status (confirmed at once). Set the largest order value, an optional advance (through Payments or recorded by your staff), a cash handling fee, whether delivery marks the order paid, and the returned-package flag, and use the blocklist in the customers admin widget. Your staff stop and restart cash on delivery for new orders with the setting Offer cash on delivery (enabled), without switching the feature (see Cash on delivery options).
delivery_zones: Delivery fees by city or area, free delivery over an amount, delivery days and store pickup, in Settings → Delivery. A shopper's address is matched to the first zone that lists its city or area.
courier_apis: Book shipments and read their status with your courier's API (see Couriers above). Connect the courier keys in Connections.
taxes: Tax rules in Settings → Taxes: a percentage per category or region, and whether your prices include tax.
coupons: Codes for a percentage or fixed amount off, with use limits, dates and conditions, made one by one or many at once (POST /v1/coupons/batch) in the promotions admin widget.
deals: Automatic offers on products, categories or brands, with conditions, days and hours, dates and use limits; shown on product cards, deal pages and in the cart (see Deal rules, deal pages and cart locks).
loyalty: Shoppers earn points, credited when the order is delivered, and redeem them at checkout. Set the earn and redeem rates, who takes part (roles and guests), what points are earned on and when they are worked out, and the expiry in Settings → Loyalty; staff adjust points in the promotions admin widget (see Loyalty options).
bundles: Bundles and buy X get Y offers, applied in the cart.
reviews: Ratings and reviews from shoppers whose order was delivered, per product or per item bought (guests too, with the order key), moderated in the customers admin widget (see Reviews per item, alerts and wishlists).
wishlist: Signed-in shoppers save products to their wishlist (wishlist widget, and the heart on product pages); POST /v1/shop/wishlist/merge adds a list your page kept for a guest.
alerts: Back-in-stock and price-drop alerts per product or variant, by email, SMS or WhatsApp through Notifications (templates ecommerce.back_in_stock and ecommerce.price_drop). Paste the Notifications token. With guests on, the product page asks a guest for a phone (with the checkout setting countries, only a phone of those countries, as for guest orders; a member's phone of another country gets no alerts); with targetPrice on, a price-drop alert may name its price. Each message's {stopUrl} opens your stop page (/alerts/unsubscribe/<token>, or the stopUrl setting with {token}): place the alerts_stop widget there. A message that reaches no one (Notifications down or refusing it) is tried again on later uses of your website, 1, 5, 15 and 60 minutes later, then marked failed; a channel that got through is never sent twice.
compare: Shoppers add products to compare and see them side by side (compare widget). The list lives in the shopper's browser.
returns: Return, exchange and warranty claims from My orders (signed in), within the windows of each item and grade, with photos (kept in your storage) and your reasons. Staff approve, receive, refund (through Payments when the order was paid online), replace, repair, restock exactly once and keep notes (see Return, exchange and warranty claims).
invoices: Invoices and packing slips with the grade, serial numbers and warranty on each line, batch packing slips and pick lists, from the orders admin widget and My orders.
csv: Import and export products and stock (with an update mode for prices and stock), and export orders and customers, as CSV in the customers admin widget.
bulk_actions: Change prices, stock, status or category for many products at once, and move many orders at once, in the admin widgets; POST /v1/data/delete-all deletes all orders, customers or the catalog.
reports: A summary with daily figures, sales by product, category, brand, city, grade and payment method, sell-through, oldest stock, stock age, return rate and margin, each also as CSV, in the customers admin widget.
seo: Meta tags, robots and structured data (ProductGroup, ItemList, and FAQPage when you ask for it) for products, categories and every listing, the sitemap and its files, default description and image, and IndexNow through Growth, served by your own site from the API (see Your site serves and Catalog and SEO).
feeds: Product feeds (XML and CSV) for shopping and social catalogs, served by your own site from the API, with your item ids, Google product category and grade labels (see Catalog and SEO).
ai_copy: Product descriptions and meta text suggested with your own OpenAI-compatible AI key (Connections → AI provider key: base URL, key and model). Suggestions are shown to staff in the catalog admin widget and never saved automatically.
llms_txt: An llms.txt of your catalog for AI assistants and, with the full setting on, llms-full.txt with every product in stock, served by your own site from the API.
size_charts: Size charts in inches or centimeters with fit advice, linked to products, brands or categories; the product page shows a Size guide (see Catalog and SEO).
landing_pages: Category, brand and grade landing pages with their own copy, indexed only while enough of their products are in stock, and attribute and grade glossary pages, all in the sitemaps (see Catalog and SEO).
role_pricing: Signed-in shoppers whose Accounts role is in the role_prices list (Settings → Role prices) get its percent off the goods, shown as its own line (see Role prices). Paste the Accounts token.
events: Your server reads the shop's events with GET /v1/events and gets them at its webhook URLs through Notifications (see Events and webhooks).
staff_alerts: Email, WhatsApp or SMS your staff about the order and claim events you choose, through Notifications (see Staff alerts).
import: For a migration only: see Import.

orderRoles: A move works only when your flow lists it for who makes it and the roles allow it (else 409 move_not_allowed). Into awaiting_payment only from open or packed: the order waits for its payment again (with the move's window option restart, the default, it gets a new time to pay; with none it waits until staff move it). Nothing moves into awaiting_confirmation. open and packed come from waiting, open or packed statuses (packed back to open frees the serial numbers captured when packing); shipped from open, packed or shipped; delivered from waiting, open, packed or shipped; cancelled from waiting, open or packed (a dispatched package is never canceled: it comes back as returned_to_origin first, and money paid can be refunded meanwhile with POST /v1/orders/<id>/refunds); returned_to_origin only from shipped; returned only from delivered; refunded from waiting, open, packed, delivered, returned_to_origin or returned. Extra moves (E40), only when you list them: cancelled from delivered or any closed status, refunded from cancelled, and between two closed statuses; what each does follows what the order still holds, so nothing is given back or taken twice. The default flow has none of the extra moves (back to waiting, packed back to open, refunded before delivery, the E40 moves) and no returned status: add the ones you use. The roles:

orderTemplates.placed: sent when an order is placed, with the name of its first status.
orderTemplates.status: sent when an order moves into a status whose notify is on (by default confirmed, dispatched, delivered, cancelled and refunded; a cancel at the end of its window too), with the checkout setting statusTemplates one (the default).
orderTemplates.perStatus: with statusTemplates per_status, the status message uses one template per status key instead (for example ecommerce.order_status.confirmed and ecommerce.order_status.dispatched in the default flow): your template for that status, else your ecommerce.order_status template, else the default words (Your order {number} is now {status}). Write one in Notifications only for the statuses that need their own words.

orderValuesIntro: Every order message gets these values, in words from your Texts (Settings → Texts), never codes; a value that does not apply is empty:

messageValues.name: the shopper's name on the order.
messageValues.firstName: the first word of that name.
messageValues.status: the status's name for the shopper (its shopperLabel, else its name; in the placed message, of its first status).
messageValues.total: the order total, written by your Format.
messageValues.paymentMethod: the payment method (texts checkout.method.cod, online, bank_transfer and pickup).
messageValues.deliveryMethod: messages.delivery.delivery or messages.delivery.pickup; empty for an order without delivery.
messageValues.courier: the courier's name once the order has a shipment.
messageValues.trackingDetails: the courier, tracking number, tracking link and tracking note that are set, joined by ·.
messageValues.orderUrl: the checkout setting orderUrl with {number} filled in.
messageValues.reviewUrl: the checkout setting reviewUrl with {number} filled in.
messageValues.cancelReason: for a cancel: the note for the shopper staff wrote with it, else the note your staff typed with it, else messages.cancelReason.staff, shopper, unpaid (not paid in time) or unconfirmed (not confirmed in time).
messageValues.shopperNote: the note for the shopper staff wrote with the move (shopperNote; empty without one).

otherTemplates: The claim and alert templates and their values. ecommerce.return_status is sent, as required, on the checkout setting messageChannels when a claim is made and at each staff step (approve, reject, receive, refund, replace, repair, close): name is the shopper's name, claim the claim's reference, kind and status are words (texts returns.kind.* and returns.status.*), reason the shopper's reason and amount the refunded amount by your Format (empty before a refund). ecommerce.back_in_stock and ecommerce.price_drop are optional messages on the alerts setting channels: name is the product's name, price its price, url its page address and stopUrl the link that stops that shopper's alerts (do not use {unsubscribeUrl} there: Notifications fills it with its own opt-out from every optional message).
staffAlerts: With Staff alerts on (it needs the Notifications token), Ecommerce tells your staff about the events the staff_alerts setting events lists (placed, cancelled, proof_uploaded and return_requested by default), as required messages saved and tried again like order messages. They go to the setting recipients (up to 20 email addresses and international phone numbers starting with + or 00; phones get WhatsApp, or SMS with phoneChannel sms) and, with staffPermission set to an Ecommerce permission (orders.read, orders.manage, orders.refund or returns.manage) and the Accounts token pasted, to every unblocked Accounts user whose role has it (their email, else their phone; read again after 5 minutes); all_staff alerts every unblocked Accounts user who works with the alert's subject: whose role may see orders (orders.read), and for a new claim whose role handles claims (returns.manage). Each address gets one message. With includePhone on, every alert also carries the shopper's phone ({phone}). Each alert goes out with Ecommerce's default words (US English) by email and SMS until you write your own template in Notifications. The templates, by event:

staffEvents.status: an order moved into another status (other than a cancel).
staffEvents.paid: an order became paid: Payments confirmed its payment (or its cash on delivery advance), your staff recorded payments that reach its total, or a move's option paidOnConfirm recorded its balance (not when delivery marks a cash order paid).
staffEvents.proof_uploaded: a shopper sent the proof of a bank transfer.
staffEvents.cancelled: your staff or the shopper canceled an order.
staffEvents.expired: an order was canceled because its time to pay or to confirm ended.
staffEvents.return_requested: a shopper made a return, exchange or warranty claim.

staffValuesIntro: Their values (each event's own ones are named above), in words like the order messages':

staffValues.name: the shopper's name.
staffValues.total: the order total, written by your Format.
staffValues.status: the name of the order's status now.
staffValues.from: the name of the status it came from.
staffValues.reference: the reference the shopper gave with the transfer proof, or the claim's reference.
staffValues.reason: why it was canceled, as cancelReason in the order messages.
staffValues.link: the staff_alerts setting adminUrl with these values filled in (for example https://admin.shop.com/orders/{id}); not sent while the setting is empty.
staffValues.phone: the phone on the order, with the staff_alerts setting includePhone on (not sent while it is off).

events: With Events on (it needs Catalog), Ecommerce records what happens in your shop for your own server: each event is { id, type, at, data, delivery }, with ids and small facts only (amounts in minor units, statuses and methods as codes; never addresses or contact details), kept 30 days. GET /v1/events?since=<ISO-8601 time>&types=<full types, comma-separated, at most 20>&cursor=&limit= lists them newest first (server token); GET /v1/events/count and /v1/events/counts?by=type|delivery count them. With the Notifications token pasted into Connections, each event is sent right after it happens to your webhook URLs by Notifications (turn on its Outgoing webhooks feature, set the URLs and the signing secret there): a POST of JSON { id, type, createdAt, websiteId, data } with the header SS-Signature (see the Notifications docs to check it). A failed send is tried again on later requests (after 1, 5 and 30 minutes and 2 hours); delivery is pending, sent, not_connected or failed. Imports record no events. Every order event's data has orderId, number, status (the status key), total, currency, paymentMethod and deliveryMethod; the types:

eventTypes.order.status_changed: { …, from, to, reason, by }: the order moved from one status key to another; reason is rto or customer_return for a package coming back, shopper or expired for those cancels, else null; by is who moved it (the staff member's name, Server for a server-token call without SS-Actor headers, system, shopper or guest).
eventTypes.order.paid: { …, paid }: the order became paid, as for the paid staff alert (also when delivery marks a cash order paid); paid is the amount paid so far.
eventTypes.order.payment_recorded: { …, method, amount, reference }: your staff recorded a payment (also through a move's paidOnConfirm, and the cash recorded when a cash order is delivered), or Payments took money outside the usual confirmation, for example after a cancel (method bank_transfer, cash, other or online). The usual Payments confirmation raises only order.paid.
eventTypes.order.proof_uploaded: { …, reference }: the shopper sent the proof of a bank transfer.
eventTypes.order.cancelled: { …, reason }: the order was canceled; reason is staff, shopper or expired (its time to pay or to confirm ended).
eventTypes.order.refunded: { …, amount, claimId }: a refund was made: with POST /v1/orders/<id>/refunds, a claim's refund (claimId, else null), a cancel that gives back what was paid online, or a move into a refunded status.
eventTypes.return.requested: { claimId, reference, kind, orderId, number }: a shopper made a claim (kind return, exchange or warranty).
eventTypes.return.status_changed: { claimId, orderId, from, to }: a claim moved (requested, approved, rejected, received, refunded, replaced, repaired or closed).
eventTypes.review.submitted: { reviewId, productId, rating, status }: a shopper wrote a review (status pending or approved, as the reviews setting moderation says).
eventTypes.catalog.changed: { kind, id, slug }: a product (kind product) was made or changed by a catalog write, or stock came back to it from an order (a cancel, a refund before delivery, a returned package or a claim's restock).
eventTypes.stock.low: { productId, variantId, stock }: an order or a catalog write dropped a variant from above the catalog setting lowStock into 1 to lowStock units (a variant offered and not marked sold out, of a product that tracks stock and is not archived, as the low-stock counts take them); a rise or a drop within the same range publishes nothing.
eventTypes.stock.out: { productId, variantId, stock }: an order or a catalog write dropped such a variant to 0 units (stock is 0).
eventTypes.settings.changed: { what, key }: a setting (key <feature>.<setting>), text, list (key the list), the theme or the Format was saved through the API or the dashboard. This one is recorded whether Events is on or not.

orders.intro: What checkout, orders and promotions can do beyond the basics, each with the feature it needs. Routes are named with the server token; most staff routes also have their /v1/admin/ twins for the admin widgets (a ticket with the permission named; not the order counter, delete-all and the lists), and the orders, promotions and customers admin widgets use them.

sections.title: Guest checkout and order keys
paragraphs: With the checkout setting guests on or unless_password, POST /v1/shop/orders takes customer { name, phone, email? } without a sign-in (see Guests, order keys and the Accounts sign-in) and answers { order, next, orderKey }. The key is shown once; the same request sent again with its Idempotency-Key within a day answers the same, key included. Send it as SS-Order-Key with GET /v1/shop/orders/<id>, GET /v1/shop/orders/by-number/<number>, POST …/cancel, …/pay, …/proof/upload, …/proof, GET …/invoice and the downloads. GET /v1/shop/orders/by-number/<number> serves an order page by its number (the owner's sign-in or the key) with the same answer as by id.

A guest is one customer record per phone (a customer id cus_… with guest true), listed and opened in the customers admin widget like a member. The blocklist and the open-order cap (the checkout setting openOrderCap: orders waiting for payment or confirmation) apply per phone, and a phone that a member's record has makes the order the member's.

sections.title: Payment, delivery and cart options
paragraphs: Checkout settings: paymentOrder (the order of the payment methods; the first available is preselected), a note per method (noteCod, noteOnline, noteBankTransfer, notePickup), addressRequired (the address fields required besides name and phone; leave out city for one free-text address), maxLines (50) and maxQuantity (99) per cart, and successUrl and cancelUrl (with {number} and {id}). Delivery settings: defaultFee and defaultFreeOver where no zone matches, defaultMethod (delivery or pickup, preselected when pickup is possible), one pickup point without Multi-location stock (pickupEnabled, pickupName, pickupAddress, pickupHours), and the notes deliveryNote, prepNote and pickupReadyNote.

Quotes answer paymentMethods (each with available, and a reason when it is not), bankDetails, notes, deliveryOptions and the pickup point; orders answer their notes, the pickup point, and bankDetails while they wait for a transfer. POST /v1/shop/orders takes expectedTotal, the total the shopper saw: a different total answers 409 price_changed with the new quote, so an offer that ended between the cart and the order never charges more. With wholeUnits on in your Format every amount Ecommerce works out is whole: the points value rounds down, percentage fees, role discounts and tax round half up, and deal discounts as the deals setting rounding says.

sections.title: Cash on delivery options
paragraphs: The cod settings: enabled (your staff stop and restart cash on delivery for new orders without switching the feature), maxOrderValue, an advance (advanceAmount, else advancePercent; paid through Payments, or with advanceVia manual by a transfer your staff record), atPickup (pay cash when collecting), feePercent with feeBase (order_total, or goods_after_discounts: the goods after deals and the role discount), added as totals.fee and printed as Cash handling, paidOnDelivery (delivering a cash on delivery or pay at pickup order records its balance as a cash payment; off: your staff record the cash) and the returned-package flag (rtoThreshold; with rtoRequireAdvance flagged customers must pay an advance).

When cash on delivery is not allowed for an order, placing it answers 422 cod_not_allowed with codReason: needs_delivery, digital_items, over_max (above maxOrderValue, with the fee) or advance_unavailable.

sections.title: Bank transfers and transfer proofs
paragraphs: With the checkout setting bankTransferVia manual, a bank-transfer order (and a cash on delivery advance with the cod setting advanceVia manual) starts awaiting payment with no Payments payment and keeps its time to pay (paymentWindowMinutes) until the shopper sends a proof: from then on it waits for your staff, who record the payment and confirm it, or cancel it. Its answers show your bank details from Payments (bankDetails, read again after 5 minutes); without Payments connected there are none, so put your account in noteBankTransfer.

The shopper sends the proof in two steps: POST /v1/shop/orders/<id>/proof/upload { type, size } (JPEG, PNG, WebP or PDF, up to 10 MB) answers { upload, key, expiresAt }, a presigned PUT to your storage valid 15 minutes; then POST /v1/shop/orders/<id>/proof { key, reference? } attaches it (it may be sent again: the last one counts) and raises order.proof_uploaded and the proof_uploaded staff alert. An order that does not wait for a manual transfer answers 409 nothing_to_pay. Your staff then record the payment (see The payments log).

sections.title: The payments log, recorded payments and refunds
paragraphs: Every order keeps payments [{ id, method, amount, reference, proofKey, note, by, at }] and refunds [{ id, method, amount, reference, claimId, note, by, at }]; payment.paid, refunded and state (unpaid, pending, paid, partially_refunded or refunded; a part payment stays unpaid) come from them, and Payments' confirmations are online entries. Staff answers add payment.balanceDue (0 on closed orders), refundable and refundDue (money left on a canceled order); shopper answers show paid, balanceDue and each entry's method, amount, reference and time, never staff names or notes.

POST /v1/orders/<id>/payments { method: bank_transfer | cash | other, amount, reference?, note?, confirm? } (orders.manage) records money your staff received, at most the balance due; it is refused on closed orders. It cancels the order's open Payments payment first (409 when the shopper paid there meanwhile, 503 while Payments cannot be reached), and confirm also moves a waiting order to the first open status staff may move it to. With a move's option paidOnConfirm (any of cod, online, bank_transfer and pickup), a staff move of a waiting order of a listed method into an open, packed or shipped status records its balance for you.

POST /v1/orders/<id>/refunds { amount, reason, method?, reference?, claimId? } (orders.refund) refunds up to what was paid less refunds. Without method (or with online) the share paid through Payments goes back through Payments first and the rest is recorded as other; bank_transfer, cash or other only record it. When Payments can only record a refund, the answer's warnings tell you to return the money by hand. The part through Payments goes through the order's refund lock: it is written on the order first, so of two refunds at once one wins (409 conflict) and every refund Payments made is recorded; when Payments does not answer, the refund is kept (refund.pending, warning refund_pending) and sent again with the same Idempotency-Key when the order is next used — do not refund it again. With the flow's refundsCover trigger, an order whose refunds reach what was paid moves to that refunded status when the flow lists the move.

sections.title: More moves, reasons and waiting again
paragraphs: POST /v1/orders/<id>/move { to, note?, shopperNote?, restock?, reason?, shipment?, serials?, video? } moves an order when your flow lists the move for staff and the roles allow it (see Order statuses and roles); add the moves you need to the order_flow list. The order's nextStatuses say what each move needs and its options. note stays with your staff; shopperNote is shown in the shopper's timeline and message (a move that needs reason refuses without it). Entering a returned_to_origin status takes reason rto (the default: counted for the customer's flag) or customer_return (not counted); both return roles put stock back as the move's restock option says (ask: send restock true or false). A move into a refunded status needs orders.refund on a ticket and refunds what is left; before delivery it needs something paid (409 nothing_paid, unless the move's unpaid is cancel) and acts as a cancel. The note for the shopper, else the note typed with a cancel, is the cancelReason of the shopper's message.

Shoppers cancel their own order with POST /v1/shop/orders/<id>/cancel along a move of your flow whose who includes shopper (by default out of awaiting payment and awaiting confirmation; any move into a canceled status before dispatch may allow it). A paid order follows that move's shopperPaid: refuse (the default out of open or packed), flag (canceled, the refund shown as due; the default out of waiting) or refund (canceled and refunded through Payments).

sections.title: Order flow options: who, needs, options, triggers and starts
paragraphs: Each move of the order_flow list is { from, to, who?, permission?, needs?, options? }; what you leave out reads as the default, which is today's behavior. who: ["staff"] (the default), ["staff", "shopper"] or ["shopper"] (only into a canceled status before dispatch; the default out of awaiting payment and awaiting confirmation) or ["system"] (only the shop itself: its triggers). permission: orders.manage, or orders.refund (always into a refunded status). needs: note (a staff note), reason (a note for the shopper) and units (every serial number before shipped or delivered; the default into shipped).

options, only those a move's kinds of step take (others are left out): paidOnConfirm (out of waiting into open, packed or shipped: the payment methods recorded as paid when staff move; default none), window (into awaiting payment: restart or none), video (into packed: off, optional or required), tracking (into shipped: required or optional), refund (into cancelled: auto or staff), shopperPaid (into cancelled with the shopper: refuse, flag or refund), unpaid (into refunded before dispatch with nothing paid: cancel with no money, the default, or refuse), restock (into returned to origin or returned: yes, no or ask; into cancelled or refunded after delivery or from a closed status: no, yes or ask) and points (into returned, and into cancelled or refunded after delivery or from a closed status: take_back or keep the earned points; redeemed points always come back). A move the shop makes by itself never asks: restock ask counts as no.

Each status is { key, label, role, shopperLabel?, shopperText?, notify? }: shoppers read shopperLabel (else label) and, under it, shopperText for their order's payment method; staff see label. triggers { paid, windowEnd, refundsCover }: Payments' confirmation moves an order to paid (an open status listed from the awaiting-payment status; '' keeps it where it is, paid), an ended window to windowEnd (a canceled status), refunds that reach what was paid to refundsCover (a refunded status listed from the order's status; '' for none, the default). starts { cod, pickup, free }: where cash on delivery, pay at pickup and free online or bank-transfer orders start (the awaiting-confirmation status by default, else the first open status; free orders may also start awaiting payment, with no time to pay).

Two checkout settings belong with the flow: editPricing (reprice, the default: a staff edit of a waiting order is priced again; keep_placed: it keeps the offer discount, delivery fee and payment fee it was placed with, the discount at most what the items come to) and deleteGivesBack (held, the default: deleting an order gives back what an order not delivered yet holds; all: a delivered or closed order also gives back the items still with the customer, its offer uses and its points).

sections.title: Changing the flow while orders are in it, and refunds that wait for Payments
paragraphs: Every way an order changes its status (staff and bulk moves, the shopper's cancel, the end of a waiting window, Payments' confirmation, a recorded payment that confirms, refunds that cover the payments) is one transaction: the order, its facts and everything it gives back or takes are written together, so of two changes at once one wins and the other gets 409 conflict.
