An order's facts (GET /v1/orders/<id>: stock held, sold, back or none; offers counted or released; redeemed points spent or given back; earned points none, credited or reversed; serial numbers captured or none) say what it holds whatever its status is called, and nothing is given back or taken twice.

Saving the order flow (Settings, or PUT /v1/lists/order_flow) is refused with 422 validation_failed (code status_in_use, naming the status and how many orders it has) when it would remove or re-key a status that has orders, or give it another role; names and moves change freely. Move its orders to another status of the same role first with POST /v1/orders/restatus { from, to }: nothing is given back or taken and no message is sent; each order's history notes it. A move of an order whose status's role was changed anyway is refused with 409 flow_changed.

The refund through Payments of a staff cancel (when its move's refund option is auto), of a shopper's cancel whose move refunds, or of a move into a refunded status runs right after the move. When Payments cannot be reached, the move is still made, the warning says so, and the refund waits in the order's effects (pending, shown as Refund waiting for Payments): it is sent again with the same Idempotency-Key when the order is opened and on use, until done; one Payments refuses is failed and refunded from the order. A refund staff make from the order first settles a waiting one (409 conflict while it runs at Payments, 503 payments_unavailable while Payments cannot tell whether it went through), so the money never goes back twice.

sections.title: Shipping, tracking notes and the dispatch video
paragraphs: Moving into a shipped status takes shipment { courier, trackingNumber, trackingNote?, estimatedDeliveryAt? } (the tracking number is required unless the move's tracking option is optional) or, with Courier APIs, { book: true, courier? }. PATCH /v1/orders/<id> with shipment changes it at any time. The courier (a key or a name from Settings → Couriers) is kept by name; shopper answers build its tracking link from today's courier list and show the tracking note and the expected date.

With the move's video option optional or required, entering a packed status takes video: an upload key in your storage, a YouTube id or address (kept as its youtube-nocookie embed address) or an https address; required refuses packing without one (422 at /video). Shopper answers and Chat's order lookups show it as the dispatch video; PATCH /v1/orders/<id> { video } replaces it while the order is packed or shipped (the history notes it). POST /v1/orders/bulk-move { to, note?, shopperNote?, restock?, ids or items: [{ id, shipment?, serials?, video? }] } moves up to 200 orders and answers each one's result.

sections.title: Editing a waiting order
paragraphs: While an order waits for payment or confirmation, has nothing paid and holds only physical items, PATCH /v1/orders/<id> also takes lines [{ variantId, quantity, unitPrice? }] (1–50), paymentMethod and delivery { method, city, area, country, locationId }. The order is priced again with the deals and coupon it was placed with (even when they have ended since), its role price and the points it used; its stock holds are swapped in one step (409 out_of_stock when there is not enough), and a Payments payment started for the old total is canceled, so the shopper pays the new one. The other PATCH fields work in more statuses: staffNote, address (while waiting, open or packed), shipment and serials.

sections.title: Order numbers and the counter
paragraphs: Order numbers take the form of the checkout setting numberPattern: {prefix}{number} (the default) is one running number, <numberPrefix><number>, for example SH-001043; {prefix}{year}-{number} starts again each year, <numberPrefix><year>-<number> with the year in your business time zone, for example SH-2026-0043. The number has at least numberDigits digits (6; 4–8), with zeros in front. A counter that does not exist yet (the running one, or a new year's) starts after the highest number already used in that form. POST /v1/orders/counter { next } (server token only; { year, next } with the yearly form) sets the next number for today's prefix; a number already used answers 422.

sections.title: Customers, seen markers and deletes
paragraphs: GET /v1/customers takes q (a name, an email, an id, or 4 or more digits of a phone), blocked, segment (guest: no Accounts user; active: at least one order; loyalty: points earned or left), createdAfter, unseen=1 and userIds; GET /v1/customers/counts?by=blocked or segment (segment counts members and guests). GET /v1/orders takes status (several, comma-separated), role, paymentState, paymentMethod (several), deliveryMethod, city, customer (cus_… or an Accounts user id), from and to (when placed), createdAfter, unseen=1 and q (number, name, email, city or phone digits).

POST /v1/orders/<id>/seen and POST /v1/customers/<id>/seen mark a record as seen by the acting user (the ticket's user, or SS-Actor-Id with the server token); unseen=1 lists what that user has not opened.

DELETE /v1/orders/<id> (orders.delete) gives back what a cancel would while the order is waiting, open, packed or shipped (a delivered or closed one too with deleteGivesBack all) and cancels its open Payments payment first (409 when it was paid meanwhile, 503 while Payments cannot be reached). The shopper's money is never deleted with it: 409 while a refund through Payments is pending for it or while an order that is not delivered still holds money (refund it first); the activity log keeps the order's number and total. POST /v1/data/delete-all { scope: catalog | orders | customers, confirm: '<your domain>' } (server token only, Bulk actions) deletes a whole scope: orders with their booked slots, coupon uses and claims (after canceling every open Payments payment and giving held stock back), customers with their loyalty accounts, or the catalog (products, categories, brands, attributes, serials, size charts and landing pages).

sections.title: Deal rules, deal pages and cart locks
paragraphs: A deal has a slug (unique, else 409 slug_taken), display fields (badgeLabel, discountLabel, color, banner, content, seo and sort), a type (percent, fixed or free_delivery) with its value on the items or the cart (target), and conditions: match all or any over rules { field: products, categories, brands, grades or attribute (with attributeId), op: in or not_in, values } and one level of groups, plus priceRange { min, max } on the variant price, minQuantity per line, cartTotal and paymentMethods. days (0 = Sunday … 6) and timeFrom and timeTo (HH:MM in your business time zone; a timeTo before timeFrom runs past midnight) limit when it applies; allowPoints false stops redeeming points, as the deals setting pointsBlockedBy says. A banner is uploaded first: POST /v1/deals/<id>/banner/upload { type, size } (JPEG, PNG, WebP or AVIF up to the catalog setting imageMaxBytes) answers { key, upload }, a presigned PUT to your storage under the deal's folder valid 15 minutes; then PATCH /v1/deals/<id> { banner: { key, alt } }. The promotions widget does both from the deal's page.

Product cards carry dealCount and their first deal's badge (deal). GET /v1/shop/deals lists the deals on now in show order (sort, then priority) and GET /v1/shop/deals/<id or slug> answers one, for a deal page; its products come from GET /v1/shop/products?deal=<id or slug>, which lists the products whose cards show the deal (its scope, and an active variant its conditions hold for). Every one of them, the cards and the product quote judge a deal as the cart does, its weekdays and hours included: a deal outside them is not shown. Quotes take paymentMethod and are priced for it. One shown price: cards, the product page (each variant's price, compareAtPrice and deal with its savings), Chat's product answers, the product quote, structured data and feeds all give the price after the best item deal on one unit as the cart prices it, with the higher price struck through; a deal that needs more than one unit, a cart total above the price or a payment method is an offer of the cart, not the price.

With the deals setting lockMinutes (0 = off), each quote line with an item deal carries a signed lock: send it back as the cart line's lock and the price is kept for that long, also when the order is placed, even if the deal ends or changes (not when it is deleted or used up). With shopperChoice, quote lines list eligibleDeals and a cart line may name its dealId. The deals settings rounding, lineChoice, cartOffer, cartThresholdBase and pointsBlockedBy choose how deals round and combine.

sections.title: Role prices
paragraphs: With Role pricing on (it needs the Accounts token), the list role_prices [{ role, percent (0–90), label }] (Settings → Role prices, or PUT /v1/lists/role_prices; up to 20) gives a signed-in shopper whose Accounts role is listed that percent off the goods after deals, bundles and coupons, before points, delivery, tax and the cash handling fee. Quotes and orders show it as totals.roleDiscount (also counted in discount) with the role's label and percent, and invoices as its own line with your label. Guests never get it.

sections.title: Loyalty options
paragraphs: The loyalty settings: roles (the Accounts roles that take part, earning and redeeming; empty = every signed-in shopper; an order a shopper of another role places earns nothing, at delivery either), guests (earn: guests earn on their phone and redeem once they sign in), earnBase (goods, or total with delivery and fees), earnAt (delivery: worked out when delivered; placement: fixed when placed), capBase, redeemMode (maximum: one switch redeems the most allowed), expiryUnit (days, or calendar months in your business time zone) and expiryRule (current: a change of the expiry applies to past points too). Points are credited when the order is delivered, and taken back when it is returned or refunded.

Quotes answer pointsToEarn. GET /v1/shop/loyalty?limit=&offset= answers balance, value, lifetimeEarned, pending (points of orders not delivered yet), history (newest first, with hasMore) and expiringSoon (points ending within 30 days). Staff read and adjust an account at /v1/loyalty/accounts/<customer id or Accounts user id>.

sections.title: Return, exchange and warranty claims
paragraphs: Signed-in shoppers claim from a delivered order of theirs: GET /v1/shop/orders/<id>/returnable shows each line's windows, photos go to your storage with POST /v1/shop/returns/photos { type, size } (JPEG, PNG or WebP), and POST /v1/shop/returns { orderId, kind, lines: [{ lineId, quantity }], reason, photos? } makes the claim. kind is one of the returns setting kinds (return and warranty; add exchange, which uses the return window); with the setting reasons the reason must be one of them, else it is free text. The reference is referencePrefix (R-) and 6 characters, kept on the claim.

Statuses: requested, approved, rejected, received, refunded, replaced, repaired and closed (rejected, replaced, repaired and closed are final). Staff approve, reject (with a note), receive { lines: [{ lineId, restock }] } (lines marked true go back to stock at once, false never), restock, refund { amount, method?, reference?, note? }, replace (exchange and warranty claims), repair (warranty claims), close, and add notes { text } that only staff see. A claim's refund is an order refund, at most what the claimed lines were paid (with the delivery fee under refundDelivery) and what is left on the order; points come back as pointsBack says (proportional, or full_refund_only). The shopper gets ecommerce.return_status at each step; a new claim raises return.requested and the return_requested staff alert.

sections.title: Reviews per item, alerts and wishlists
paragraphs: With the reviews setting per order_line, a review is per item bought: POST /v1/shop/reviews { orderId, lineId, rating, title?, body? } from the order's owner, or a guest with its SS-Order-Key, once the order is delivered (one per line, else 409 already_reviewed). With per product (the default) a signed-in shopper with a delivered order of the product sends { productId, rating, title?, body? }. Answers carry verified and the variant name; nameFormat first_initial shows names as Alex K. (also in the structured data), and pageSize sets the page. Staff approve, reject, set back to pending (POST /v1/reviews/<id>/pending), reply and delete, and /v1/reviews/counts?by=status counts them.

Alerts are per product or variant: POST /v1/shop/alerts { kind: back_in_stock | price_drop, productId, variantId?, targetPrice? }. A price-drop alert may name a price below today's (the product page asks for it with the alerts setting targetPrice); with the setting guests a guest gives phone instead of signing in. Each alert message's {stopUrl} opens your stop page, which calls POST /v1/shop/alerts/unsubscribe/<token>: it removes every alert of that email or phone and answers { removed } (0 for an unknown token). Alerts are also sent when stock comes back from an order (a cancel, a refund before delivery, a returned package or a claim's restock). POST /v1/shop/wishlist/merge { productIds } adds a list your page kept for a guest to the signed-in shopper's wishlist (up to 200).

sections.title: Invoices, batch packing slips and pick lists
paragraphs: Invoices show each line's grade, serial numbers and warranty days, the offer discount, member discount, points, delivery, cash handling fee and tax apart, the payment and refund entries, and Cash due on delivery for unpaid cash on delivery orders, in the words of the invoices settings. GET /v1/orders/packing-slips?ids=<up to 50, comma-separated> gives one printable HTML page with a slip per order (with the cash to collect and empty serial slots), and GET /v1/orders/pick-list?ids=<up to 100> the units to pick per variant with their order numbers; an unknown id refuses the whole request (404). Shoppers get their invoice from GET /v1/shop/orders/<id>/invoice, with the shopper's sign-in or a guest order's key (SS-Order-Key); with the invoices setting shopperFrom confirmed, only once the order is confirmed. The order's invoice field says whether it can be read now.

sections.title: Reports and CSV
paragraphs: Reports take from and to (YYYY-MM-DD in your business time zone, or ISO times; the last 30 days by default, at most 366) and count the orders placed then, not canceled, in your currency. GET /v1/reports/summary?statuses=&series=day answers { orders, total, goods, delivery, fees, discount, refunded, units, days: [{ day, orders, total }] } (statuses: the status keys that count, instead of every status but canceled). /v1/reports/sales?by= takes product, category, brand, city, grade or payment_method; /v1/reports/sell-through gives per product the units sold over sold plus stock left; /v1/reports/oldest-stock each active variant with stock, by its last sale. Every report takes format=csv (a file download).

GET /v1/reports/health answers shop health, judged on each read: { checks: [{ key, status, count, link }], attention } with the checks products_without_photos (active), images_short_lived (storage connected but no public address of your images: the widgets show them through links that last an hour; skipped without storage), archived_featured, variants_out_of_stock and variants_low_stock (the catalog setting lowStock), business_name (business.json), website_address, payment_methods (none shoppers can use) and pixel_ids (tag ids in Growth not in their form; skipped until the Growth token is pasted in Connections). status is ok, attention or skipped; link is the list that shows them, such as /v1/products?lowStock=1. The customers admin widget shows it as a card above the reports.

GET /v1/csv/orders?per=order gives one row per order instead of per line, with the order list's filters (at most 10,000 orders); GET /v1/csv/customers lists customers (at most 20,000). The product export ends with sold_out and updated_at: POST /v1/csv/products?mode=update { csv, dryRun } with such a file changes only price, stock and sold_out (empty cells keep the value) and refuses rows whose updated_at is older than the product's (export it again). Every CSV import is a dry run unless dryRun is false; the csv setting delimiter sets the separator.

import.intro: Moving a shop in from another system: with the Import feature on (our admins switch it on for a migration and off after it), your server sends the records with ss-import or your own script. Only the server token works. An import sends no message, event, alert or IndexNow call, and holds no stock, slot, offer use or points.

sections.title: Import routes
paragraphs: POST /v1/import/<collection> takes NDJSON (Content-Type application/x-ndjson, one record per line, at most 1,000 records or 4 MB per call; ?dryRun=1 checks everything, uniqueness too, without writing) in Ecommerce's own stored shapes: given ids (<prefix>_ and 10–64 lower-case letters or digits, for example prd_ and the old 24-hex id), times as ISO-8601 text, money in minor units and storage keys for media (copy the files into your bucket first). Each record is found by its key (id; customerId for loyalty, userId for wishlists) and replaced whole when it is there already, so a second run gives the source again.

Unknown fields, websiteId and merchantId, values the shop works out itself (a category's path; a product's price, priceMax, inStock, stockState and grades) and text over a limit are refused by path (never cut), as are catalog references to records not imported yet and slugs, SKUs, serial numbers or order numbers another record holds. The answer is { inserted, updated, failed, dryRun }, failed listing each refused line { line, id, errors: [{ path, message }] }.

POST /v1/import/<collection>/prune { keep: [keys], after?, through? } removes the records an import wrote whose keys are not kept (records made in Ecommerce stay), at most 1,000 per call (more: true: call again). GET /v1/import/status answers { collections, imported, totals }: the counts and sums ss-import verify compares.

sections.title: What to send, in order
paragraphs: The catalog first: size_charts (szc_), categories (cat_), brands (brd_), attributes (att_), landings (lnd_), products (prd_, variants var_), serials (ser_), deals (deal_) and bundles (bnd_); then customers (cus_), orders (ord_), loyalty, reviews (rev_), returns (ret_), alerts (alr_) and wishlists. A catalog record may name only records of the collections before it (a category's parent may come later). Coupons are not imported.

Taken as given: ids, numbers, createdAt, publishedAt, used, sold, rating, previousSlugs, stock and past times. A product may carry feedGroupId and a variant feedId: the item group and item ids the earlier shop's product feed used (1 to 50 letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores), so shopping catalogs keep listing the same items; only an import sets them. An order keeps its number (in your numberPattern's form: <numberPrefix><digits>, or <numberPrefix><year>-<digits>), status (a key of your order flow, with that status's role) and history (an entry's shopperNote, the note the shopper was shown, stays in their timeline), its payments and refunds (paid and refunded must be their sums, so an order paid through a gateway you no longer use comes in with an other entry that names it in reference or note), stockHeld and pointsCredited, and its totals must add up as checkout adds them. A guest customer has a name and an E.164 phone (one guest per phone); a loyalty account gives its lots and history (its balance is worked out). Imported alerts are never due.

sections.title: Finish
paragraphs: After the records, POST /v1/import/finish works out what the shop derives, in batches, writing only what changed, so a second run changes nothing: each category's path (orphans, cycles and too-deep ones are listed), each product's price, highest price, stock state and grades; each customer's order count, returned packages and last order; loyalty balances and lifetime points; products' sold (units of delivered orders) and rating (approved reviews) where they have order lines or reviews; the serials sold on the order lines that still hold them; and each order-number counter, so the next order gets the number after the highest. One call works on at most 200 records and answers what it checked and changed: while it answers more, call again with ?after=<next> (ss-import send does).

build.catalog:
Add the widget script with your browser token to every page (Install and tokens in the Portal). Make product pages at your product address (catalog setting productUrl, /products/{slug} by default) holding
, and category pages at categoryUrl (/categories/{slug}) holding
; or build your own from GET /v1/shop/products and GET /v1/shop/products/. Connect Storage and allow PUT and GET from your website and your admin in the bucket's CORS. Until mediaBaseUrl names your bucket's public address, serve your images' lasting addresses at mediaPath (/media) with the media route (Your site serves). In your admin, the catalog_admin widget with tickets from your server.
build.variants: Nothing more on your pages: the product page widget shows the variant picker with each variant's photos, price and stock; your own pages read the variants (each with its url, price and compareAtPrice) from GET /v1/shop/products/<id or slug>. With the catalog setting variantQuery (for example grade={grade}&{attributes}) each variant has its own address, which links, sitemaps, feeds and structured data use: your product page answers at its product's address whatever the query, and the widget opens the variant the query names (your own page compares the variants' url).
build.size_charts: Nothing on your pages: the product page widget shows the Size guide of the product, else its brand's, its category's or the default chart (size_charts setting defaultChartId); your own pages read it as sizeChart in GET /v1/shop/products/<id or slug>. Add charts in the catalog admin widget or with POST /v1/size-charts from your server.
build.multi_location: Nothing on your pages. Add your warehouses and shops in the catalog admin widget or with POST /v1/locations, and their stock there or with POST /v1/products/<id>/stock and a locationId from your server; orders take stock from the first location that has it, in your order, and a location marked for pickup is a pickup point at checkout.
build.grades_serials: Nothing more on your pages: the product page widget shows each variant's grade with its color, condition video and text. Define your grades in Settings → Grades and serials (or PUT /v1/lists/grades); register serial numbers in the catalog admin widget or with POST /v1/serials, and staff pick them when an order is packed (orders_admin widget). For grade glossary pages, see Landing pages.
build.digital_goods: Connect Storage (files are kept in your bucket) and attach files or license keys to products in the catalog admin widget, or with POST /v1/products/<id>/files and /licences from your server. Nothing more on your pages: once the order is paid, My orders (my_orders widget) gives the shopper the download links and keys; your own pages download with GET /v1/shop/orders/<id>/downloads/<line id>/<file>, with the sign-in or a guest's SS-Order-Key.
build.bookings: Set your weekly booking hours in Settings → Catalog (or PUT /v1/lists/booking_hours) and a duration on each service product. Nothing more on your pages: the product page widget shows the free slots and the cart books the one chosen; your own pages read slots from GET /v1/shop/slots and send the slot with the cart line.
build.checkout:
Place
on your cart page and
on an orders page; your header can show SSEcommerce.cart.count(). Pass the shopper's Accounts sign-in with SSEcommerce.identify(signIn) (paste your Accounts server token into Connections), or let guests order (checkout setting guests). For online payments and bank transfers paste your Payments server token: shoppers come back to the cart's own page (or successUrl) with ?ss_order=. Your policy pages read GET /v1/policies from your server. Set your order flow, couriers and messages in Settings; in your admin, the orders_admin and customers_admin widgets with tickets from your server.
build.cod: Nothing on your pages: the cart widget offers cash on delivery with your note (noteCod), its fee and any advance, and your own checkout reads them from POST /v1/shop/cart/quote. Set the largest order value, the advance and the cash handling fee in Settings; staff confirm new orders and keep the blocklist in the orders_admin and customers_admin widgets.
build.delivery_zones: Nothing on your pages: the cart widget asks for the address, matches it to the first zone that lists its city or area, and shows the fee, the delivery days, free delivery over your amount and store pickup. Add your zones in Settings → Delivery (or PUT /v1/lists/delivery_zones) and the default fee for addresses no zone matches; your own checkout reads deliveryOptions from POST /v1/shop/cart/quote.
build.courier_apis: Nothing on your pages. Paste your courier's booking and tracking addresses, key and body template into Connections (Courier API keys); staff book a shipment when an order ships (orders_admin widget, or a move with shipment { book: true } from your server), and shoppers see the tracking link and the latest status in My orders. There is nothing to register at the courier.
build.taxes: Nothing on your pages: the cart, orders and invoices show tax as your rules say. Add your rules (a percentage per category or region) in Settings → Taxes (or PUT /v1/lists/tax_rules) and say whether your prices include tax (pricesIncludeTax).
build.coupons: Nothing more on your pages: the cart widget has the coupon box; your own checkout sends coupon with POST /v1/shop/cart/quote and the order. Make codes one by one or many at once in the promotions_admin widget, or with POST /v1/coupons and /v1/coupons/batch from your server.
build.deals:
Nothing more on your pages: cards and the product page show each deal's badge and the price after it, struck through, and the cart applies it. For a deal page, read GET /v1/shop/deals/ and list its products with
; GET /v1/shop/deals lists the deals on now. Make deals in the promotions_admin widget or with POST /v1/deals from your server.
build.loyalty: Nothing more on your pages: the cart widget shows the points to earn and lets signed-in shoppers redeem them, and My orders shows the balance. A points page of your own reads GET /v1/shop/loyalty. Set the rates and expiry in Settings → Loyalty; staff adjust points in the promotions_admin widget.
build.role_pricing: Paste your Accounts server token into Connections and pass the shopper's sign-in with SSEcommerce.identify(signIn). List the Accounts roles and their percent off in Settings → Role prices (or PUT /v1/lists/role_prices); the cart, orders and invoices then show the member discount as its own line. Nothing more on your pages.
build.bundles: Nothing on your pages: the cart applies your bundles and buy X get Y offers and shows what they save. Make them in the promotions_admin widget or with POST /v1/bundles from your server.
build.reviews: Nothing more on your pages: the product page widget shows the reviews and, for a signed-in shopper with a delivered order, the form to write one. Your own pages read GET /v1/shop/products/<id>/reviews and send POST /v1/shop/reviews (with the reviews setting per order_line, per item bought, guests too with their SS-Order-Key); with the checkout setting reviewUrl, order messages link to your review page. Staff moderate and reply in the customers_admin widget.
build.wishlist:
Place
on a wishlist page; the product page widget has the heart. Shoppers sign in with Accounts (pass the sign-in with SSEcommerce.identify(signIn)); a list your page kept for a guest joins their wishlist with POST /v1/shop/wishlist/merge.
build.alerts:
Paste your Notifications server token into Connections: ecommerce.back_in_stock and ecommerce.price_drop go out with Ecommerce's default words by email and SMS until you write your own templates in Notifications (WhatsApp needs your approved template). The product page widget offers the alerts; make a stop page at /alerts/unsubscribe/ (or the alerts setting stopUrl) holding
.
build.compare:
Place
on a compare page; product cards and the product page add to it, and the list lives in the shopper's browser. Your own page reads GET /v1/shop/compare?ids=.
build.returns: Nothing more on your pages: signed-in shoppers make return, exchange and warranty claims from My orders (my_orders widget), with photos kept in your storage (connect Storage). Set the windows, kinds and reasons in Settings → Returns; staff handle claims in the orders_admin widget or with the /v1/returns routes from your server.
build.invoices: Nothing more on your pages: My orders links each order's invoice (GET /v1/shop/orders/<id>/invoice, with the sign-in or a guest's SS-Order-Key). Staff print invoices, packing slips and pick lists from the orders_admin widget, or your server reads GET /v1/orders/<id>/invoice, /packing-slips and /pick-list. Change the words in Settings → Invoices.
build.csv: Nothing on your pages: staff import and export products and stock, and export orders and customers, in the customers_admin widget; your server uses GET and POST /v1/csv/products, GET /v1/csv/orders and GET /v1/csv/customers.
build.bulk_actions: Nothing on your pages: staff change many products at once in the catalog_admin widget and move many orders at once in the orders_admin widget; your server uses POST /v1/products/bulk and POST /v1/orders/bulk-move.
build.reports: Nothing on your pages: staff read the reports in the customers_admin widget; your server reads GET /v1/reports/summary, /sales, /sell-through, /oldest-stock, /stock-age, /returns, /margin and /health (each also as CSV).
build.events: On your server: read the events with GET /v1/events (server token), or paste your Notifications server token into Connections and turn on Outgoing webhooks in Notifications with your webhook URLs to receive each one as it happens, signed with SS-Signature. Each event carries ids and small facts; read the record itself from the API.
build.staff_alerts: Nothing on your pages. Paste your Notifications server token into Connections and choose the events and recipients in Settings → Staff alerts; the ecommerce.staff_<event> messages go out with Ecommerce's default words by email and SMS until you write your own templates in Notifications (WhatsApp needs your approved template). With adminUrl (with {number} or {id}) each alert links to the order in your admin.
build.seo: In the head of each product, category and listing page, put the SEO answer your server fetches with the server token: GET /v1/seo/products/<slug>, GET /v1/seo/categories/<slug> or GET /v1/seo/listing?category=<slug>&<the rest of your page's query> answer the title, description, canonical, robots and the JSON-LD for a script tag; an answer { moved } is a 308 to its url. Serve your sitemap at the seo setting sitemapUrl (/sitemap.xml) with the sitemap route (Your site serves) and name it in robots.txt.
build.landing_pages: Serve your landing pages at the landing_pages setting landingUrl (by default your category page with ?brand= and &grade=): the listing's head and intro come from GET /v1/seo/listing with that query. For glossary pages, set attributeUrl and gradeUrl and serve them from GET /v1/seo/attributes/<slug> and GET /v1/seo/grades/<key>. All of them are in your sitemap.
build.feeds: Serve /feeds/products.xml and /feeds/products.csv from your domain with the feed routes (Your site serves: they fetch GET /v1/feeds/products.xml and .csv with the server token), then give those addresses to Google Merchant Center and Meta Commerce Manager as scheduled feeds.
build.ai_copy: Nothing on your pages. Save your OpenAI-compatible provider (base URL, key and model) in Connections (AI provider key); staff ask for suggestions in the catalog_admin widget, or your server calls POST /v1/products/<id>/ai-copy and POST /v1/landings/<id>/ai-copy. Suggestions are never saved by themselves.
build.llms_txt: Serve /llms.txt from your domain with the llms.txt route (Your site serves: it fetches GET /v1/llms.txt with the server token) and, with the llms_txt setting full on, /llms-full.txt from GET /v1/llms-full.txt.
build.import: Nothing on your pages: for a migration only, run ss-import with your server token against the /v1/import routes (see Import), then switch the feature off.
